intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) — DXd bystander mechanism
model_system: HER2-positive/HER2-negative tumor cell cocultures (KPL-4 + MDA-MB-468) and mixed-cell mouse xenografts (NCI-N87 + MDA-MB-468-Luc)
control_arm: T-DM1 and an anti-HER2 ADC carrying a low-permeability DXd conjugate
mechanism: The released DXd payload crosses membranes into neighboring cells, so killing is not confined to cells that internalize the ADC.
key_finding: DS-8201a killed HER2-negative cells cocultured with HER2-positive cells, while T-DM1 and a low-permeability DXd conjugate did not. In mixed NCI-N87/MDA-MB-468-Luc xenografts DS-8201a suppressed the HER2-negative luciferase signal. HER2-negative tumors implanted on the contralateral flank were unaffected, placing the effect at the range of a few cell diameters.
caveats: Breast and gastric lines only, no urothelial model. The bystander range is local, so it rescues heterogeneous or antigen-low tumor rather than antigen-null tumor — a distinction that matters if the current node has genuinely lost HER2.

intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) in HER2 IHC 1+/2+, FISH-negative tumor
model_system: primary FISH-negative endometrial carcinoma cell lines (HER2 IHC 0, 1+, 2+) and HER2 IHC 1+ and 2+ xenografts
control_arm: non-binding control ADC
mechanism: HER2 binding at low receptor density still delivers enough DXd to trigger double-strand breaks, supplemented by bystander transfer and ADCC.
key_finding: T-DXd was cytotoxic against IHC 1+ and 2+ FISH-negative lines but not against the IHC 0 line, where killing matched the control ADC. Both IHC 2+ and IHC 1+ xenografts showed growth suppression and longer survival.
caveats: Endometrial models, not urothelial, and the IHC 0 result marks the floor: activity tracked expression tier rather than being independent of it. If repeat validated IHC returns HER2-low rather than 3+, this is the evidence base — weaker and less predictive of benefit than the IHC 3+ data behind the tumor-agnostic approval.

intervention_label: HER2-directed ADCs — polyploid giant cancer cell persister resistance
model_system: HER2-amplified breast (JIMT-1) and gastric (MKN7, SNU-216) lines; SCID mouse xenografts
control_arm: untreated cells and cross-comparison among four HER2 ADCs
dose_and_schedule: trastuzumab emtansine, trastuzumab deruxtecan, XMT-1522 and disitamab vedotin, as published
mechanism: ADC exposure selects drug-tolerant polyploid giant cells that downregulate HER2 protein and upregulate nectin-4, moving the vulnerable antigen from one target to another.
key_finding: All four HER2 ADCs induced polyploid giant cancer cells whose daughter cells carried reduced HER2 protein; JIMT-1 lost the HER2 amplicon after XMT-1522. Those persister populations upregulated nectin-4, and enfortumab vedotin blocked regrowth of JIMT-1 xenografts.
caveats: Breast and gastric lines, and the ADC-to-persister sequence is the reverse of this patient's history (EV first, then T-DXd). The morphologic overlap is still hard to ignore: pleomorphic giant cells were described in the 2025 recurrence, and the model predicts exactly the HER2-down/nectin-4-up pattern the 2026-08 MXIF discordance raises.

exclusion_reason: Activity in this model is driven by activating ERBB2 mutation rather than by expression tier; the patient's ERBB2 mutation status is not in the record, and the case question is whether HER2 protein is retained.
intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan in ERBB2-mutated, HER2-low cervical carcinoma
enfortumab vedotin — antigen retention and P-glycoprotein-mediated resistance
model_system: breast cancer mouse model treated with an EV-like anti-nectin-4 MMAE ADC (N41mab-vcMMAE) to acquired resistance
control_arm: resistant tumors treated with ADC alone; tariquidar plus docetaxel as a comparator combination
dose_and_schedule: 9 months of continuous N41mab-vcMMAE treatment; tariquidar combined with the ADC at rechallenge
mechanism: Resistance arose through focal ABCB1 amplification and P-glycoprotein overexpression, which pumps MMAE out of the cell while nectin-4 stays on the surface.
key_finding: RNA sequencing of resistant tumors showed ABCB1 upregulation with focal gene amplification and high P-gp protein. Pharmacologic P-gp inhibition restored sensitivity in vitro, and tariquidar plus the ADC produced rapid regression of resistant tumors in mice, whereas tariquidar plus docetaxel was toxic and largely ineffective.
caveats: Breast model with an EV-like surrogate rather than clinical EV in urothelial tissue. The load-bearing point for this case is that resistance was a payload-efflux problem, not antigen loss — which argues for keeping nectin-4 on the target list but changing the payload class.

intervention_label: enfortumab vedotin — NECTIN4 expression as the sensitivity determinant
model_system: seven muscle-invasive bladder cancer transcriptomic cohorts plus luminal and basal bladder cancer cell lines with NECTIN4 overexpression or knockdown
control_arm: isogenic parental lines
mechanism: NECTIN4 sits downstream of luminal differentiation (GATA3, FOXA1, PPARG), and surface density sets how much MMAE reaches the cell.
key_finding: NECTIN4 expression was heterogeneous across consensus molecular subtypes and enriched in luminal tumors. Knockdown conferred EV resistance and overexpression conferred sensitivity in both luminal and basal lines, making expression both necessary and sufficient.
caveats: Cell-line manipulation rather than post-EV patient tissue, and subtype was not assigned for this patient. It is the reason a contemporary nectin-4 stain, not the 2023 result, is the decision-relevant test.

intervention_label: NECTIN4-directed CAR T cells, with PPARγ-agonist antigen priming
model_system: bladder cancer cell lines across a range of endogenous NECTIN4, EV-resistant derivatives, and a post-EV patient biopsy cohort
control_arm: untransduced T cells; NECTIN4-low versus NECTIN4-high targets
dose_and_schedule: rosiglitazone priming before CAR T coculture
mechanism: PPARγ transcriptionally controls NECTIN4, so a PPARγ agonist raises surface antigen; CAR T killing engages antigen directly rather than requiring internalization of a payload.
key_finding: NECTIN4-CAR T cells killed across a range of endogenous NECTIN4 levels, with greater activity against high expressors, and rosiglitazone priming raised NECTIN4 and increased killing. EV-resistant cells remained susceptible, and the post-EV biopsy cohort largely retained NECTIN4 expression.
caveats: No NECTIN4 CAR T product is open to this patient, so the transferable finding is the antigen-retention observation in post-EV human biopsies, which bears on every nectin-4 re-targeting option including the AKY-1189 radioligand and the topoisomerase-payload ADCs.

intervention_label: enfortumab vedotin — uptake-defective resistance with retained NECTIN4
model_system: paired pre- and post-treatment spatial transcriptomics of NECTIN4-ADC plus anti-PD-1-treated tumors, humanized mouse models, scRNA-seq, and resistant cell systems
control_arm: pre-treatment paired tumors and parental cell lines
mechanism: AKR1C1 binds NECTIN4 and blocks AP2M1-dependent clathrin-mediated internalization, while an AKR1C1-WWP2 axis exports the ADC in extracellular vesicles, so payload never accumulates intracellularly.
key_finding: The resistant tumor-cell state carried increased NECTIN4 but defective ADC uptake. Inhibiting AKR1C1 restored internalization, raised intracellular payload and re-sensitized preclinical models.
caveats: No AKR1C1 inhibitor is clinically available. The value here is the second independent line of evidence that post-EV progression can occur with antigen intact, which means a negative functional response to EV does not by itself predict failure of a non-internalizing nectin-4 agent.

intervention_label: ETx-22 (nectin-4-directed ADC, exatecan payload)
model_system: patient-derived xenografts spanning low to high nectin-4, an MMAE-resistant xenograft, and non-human primate toxicology
control_arm: MMAE-based enfortumab-vedotin-like ADC
dose_and_schedule: highest non-severely toxic dose above 20 mg/kg in non-human primates
mechanism: An exatecan topoisomerase I payload with a membrane-permeable released species kills at lower antigen occupancy than MMAE and is not a P-glycoprotein substrate to the same degree.
key_finding: ETx-22 produced rapid, durable regressions in PDX models across low to high nectin-4 and in a monomethyl auristatin E-resistant xenograft. Non-human primate tolerability exceeded 20 mg/kg without significant skin toxicity.
caveats: PubMed carries only the significance statement; response rates by model and group sizes were read from the PMC full text summary, and no per-arm n is stated there. ETx-22 is not itself on offer — this is class read-across to LY4052031 (camptothecin payload) and AVZO-103 (exatecan payload), and it is the closest preclinical answer to whether a non-MMAE nectin-4 ADC works after EV.

intervention_label: Nectin-4 x TROP2 bispecific drug conjugate (dtNDC, eribulin payload)
model_system: three human tumor xenograft models (including MDA-MB-468 and HCC1954) in mice
control_arm: unconjugated and non-fatty-acid-modified formats; vehicle
dose_and_schedule: two subcutaneous or two intravenous doses; 20-h plasma half-life, tumor uptake peaking 2 h after IV injection
mechanism: Dual Nectin-4 and TROP2 binding raises the fraction of tumor cells engaged when either antigen alone is patchy, and the Fc-free nanobody format improves tumor penetration.
key_finding: Two subcutaneous doses rendered all MDA-MB-468 tumor-bearing mice tumor-free, and two intravenous doses produced complete remission in HCC1954 xenografts. Liver, lung, kidney and heart histology showed no treatment-related injury at therapeutic doses.
caveats: Breast xenografts, a nanobody-eribulin conjugate rather than an exatecan ADC, and no arm stratified by low antigen. It supports the dual-antigen concept behind AVZO-103 but not the specific payload or the antigen-low case that matters here.

intervention_label: NECTIN4 amplification and protein expression across urothelial subtypes and nodal metastases
model_system: cystectomy tissue microarrays with paired pelvic lymph node metastases; FISH and IHC
n_units: n=841 patients; n=218 with paired nodal metastasis
mechanism: 1q23.3 amplification containing NECTIN4 raises protein expression, but copy number and protein are only loosely coupled and both vary by histologic subtype and by site.
key_finding: NECTIN4 amplification was present in 18% of urothelial carcinomas and 19% of plasmacytoid carcinomas, and amplified tumors carried significantly higher H scores (P < 0.0001). Primary-to-node agreement for IHC was only moderate (kappa = 0.41), with amplified primaries occasionally paired to unamplified or low-expressing metastases.
caveats: Descriptive pathology with no therapeutic arm, and the cohort is treatment-naive rather than post-EV. It quantifies the specific risk in this case: a 2023 bladder and liver result does not reliably predict expression in a 2026 para-aortic node, independent of any EV effect.

exclusion_reason: Near-infrared photoimmunotherapy needs light delivered to the lesion, which is not deliverable to a retroperitoneal node and matches no option in this case's trial set.
intervention_label: Nectin-4-targeted near-infrared photoimmunotherapy

exclusion_reason: Restricted to central nervous system metastases, a site this patient does not have, and published as a letter without a therapeutic arm.
intervention_label: NECTIN4 amplification in CNS metastases of urothelial carcinoma
datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) — bystander killing of TROP2-negative tumor
model_system: nine primary poorly differentiated endometrial carcinoma cell lines stratified by flow-cytometry TROP2, admixed TROP2-positive/TROP2-negative cocultures, and chemotherapy-resistant xenografts
control_arm: non-binding control ADC
mechanism: DXd released inside TROP2-positive cells diffuses into adjacent TROP2-negative cells, adding double-strand breaks and ADCC to direct killing.
key_finding: Seven of nine primary lines expressed TROP2, and TROP2-positive lines were significantly more sensitive to Dato-DXd than to control ADC. Admixture with TROP2-positive cells produced significant bystander killing of TROP2-negative tumor, and xenograft growth inhibition was significant (P < 0.0001).
caveats: Endometrial, not urothelial, and the sensitivity contrast still ran along the expression axis — bystander killing was shown for negative cells adjacent to high expressors, not for a uniformly weak-expressing tumor. Weak TROP2 on research-grade MXIF is therefore a much less reliable predictor of benefit than the strong expression these models carry.

intervention_label: ADC payload sensitivity (MMAE, SN-38) under DNA repair deficiency in bladder cancer
model_system: isogenic bladder cancer cell line pairs with and without homologous recombination or nucleotide excision repair deficiency
control_arm: repair-proficient isogenic parental lines
dose_and_schedule: free payload exposure (MMAE, SN-38) alone or with PARP, ATR or USP1 inhibitors
mechanism: Topoisomerase I trapping by SN-38 and mitotic damage from MMAE both leave lesions that homologous recombination normally resolves, so HR loss lowers the tolerated payload dose.
key_finding: BRCA2 loss produced an HR-deficient phenotype and raised sensitivity to cisplatin, PARP inhibition, MMAE and SN-38; NER deficiency did not. SN-38 combined with PARP inhibition was synergistic irrespective of HR or NER status.
caveats: Isogenic lines only, no in-vivo arm, and ARID1A was not among the repair genes tested — the read-across to this patient's ARID1A loss is inference, not measurement. The retrievable NGS report and somatic HR-gene status would decide whether it applies at all.

exclusion_reason: Characterizes an investigational epitope-distinct TROP2 ADC (R7059-DXd) with no clinical program this patient could enter; the TROP2-variant binding finding does not change any option on the current list.
intervention_label: R7059-DXd (epitope-distinct TROP2 ADC)
mesothelin-based CAR T cells in bladder cancer models
model_system: multiple bladder cancer cell lines, patient-derived bladder tumor organoids, and xenograft bladder cancer models
control_arm: untransduced T cells; intravenous versus intravesical delivery
dose_and_schedule: intravesical instillation compared with intravenous adoptive transfer
mechanism: A second-generation CAR built on the mesothelin scaffold engages MUC16, the physiologic mesothelin ligand, on bladder tumor cells.
key_finding: MSLN-28z CAR T cells were active across bladder cancer lines and patient-derived organoids, and MUC16 was enriched in tumors refractory to existing therapy. Intravesical delivery gave better tumor control than intravenous transfer while limiting systemic T-cell engraftment.
caveats: The target engaged is MUC16, not mesothelin itself, and the delivery route was intravesical — designed for organ-confined disease, not a para-aortic node. It is the strongest bladder-specific mesothelin-scaffold data available and it does not transfer directly to systemic mesothelin CAR T dosing.

intervention_label: juxtamembrane ('stump')-targeting mesothelin CAR T cells
model_system: ovarian and pancreatic tumor lines, plus a human mesothelin knock-in mouse model
control_arm: conventional membrane-distal anti-mesothelin CARs (SS1, M5 lineage)
mechanism: Most surface mesothelin is proteolytically shed, leaving a juxtamembrane stump; a binder against the stump neither loses its epitope to shedding nor gets decoyed by soluble mesothelin in serum.
key_finding: CAR 422 T cells matched conventional anti-mesothelin CARs for cytotoxicity and in-vivo activity, and retained activity against tumor cells resistant to the conventional CARs. On-target off-tumor toxicity was lower in the human mesothelin knock-in mouse.
caveats: Ovarian and pancreatic models, no urothelial data, and CAR 422 is not in a trial this patient could enter. It does explain why serum soluble mesothelin is worth measuring before any mesothelin-directed product, and why binder epitope should be read off each protocol.

intervention_label: M7A-DC / M7GA-DC (mesothelin-directed DARPin-MMAE conjugates)
model_system: 3D tumor spheroids and pancreatic cancer mouse models with limited mesothelin expression
control_arm: conventional full-size mesothelin ADCs; PD-1 blockade alone
mechanism: A DARPin against the protease-sensitive C-terminal region of mesothelin is internalized and releases MMAE, which then kills adjacent mesothelin-negative cells; the small format penetrates spheroids better than an IgG-based ADC.
key_finding: Both conjugates were internalized by mesothelin-positive cells and produced bystander killing of mesothelin-negative cells. M7GA-DC improved tumor control and survival in pancreatic models with limited mesothelin, and adding PD-1 blockade generated durable immunologic memory.
caveats: Pancreatic models and a preclinical-only agent. Worth flagging against this patient's constraints rather than for them: the payload is MMAE, the same class that drove his chronic neuropathy on enfortumab vedotin.

intervention_label: mesothelin x CD3 T-cell engager (LABC-13F08 BiTE and BiTE-secreting T cells)
model_system: MSLN-positive ovarian, mesothelioma and pancreatic cell lines; NSG mice xenografted with the same, using transduced primary human T cells
control_arm: untransduced primary T cells; monovalent BiTE versus BiTE-secreting T cells
mechanism: A bispecific engager crosslinks CD3 on T cells to surface mesothelin; T cells engineered to secrete it locally sustain the engager concentration inside the tumor.
key_finding: The monovalent BiTE was potent in vitro, and BiTE-secreting T cells controlled ovarian and mesothelioma xenografts with some monotherapy control in a pancreatic model. The secreted engager recruited non-engineered bystander T cells and drove activation-dependent killing of cells lacking mesothelin, and an inducible off-switch cleared the engineered cells.
caveats: No urothelial model, and the specific construct differs from CT-95. The antigen-independent bystander killing reported here cuts both ways — it may cover heterogeneous expression, and it is also a plausible source of off-tumor toxicity.

intervention_label: DS-3939a (TA-MUC1-directed ADC, DXd payload)
model_system: clinical tumor tissue microarrays across cancer types, TA-MUC1-positive cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts
control_arm: isotype control ADC; xenografts pretreated with other cytotoxic ADCs
mechanism: The antibody reads the aberrantly glycosylated tumor-associated MUC1 glycoform rather than MUC1 protein per se, which is what separates tumor from the ubiquitous normal-tissue expression; the DXd payload then induces DNA damage and apoptosis.
key_finding: Tissue microarray staining put bladder among the highest TA-MUC1-positive rates, alongside lung and breast. DS-3939a inhibited growth of TA-MUC1-positive cells in vitro and caused regression in cell-line and patient-derived xenografts, including models previously exposed to other cytotoxic ADCs.
caveats: Bladder appears in the expression survey but the efficacy models are not urothelial, and DS-3939a is in phase I/II (NCT05875168) rather than on this patient's trial list. The glycoform point is the actionable one: the 2026-08 MXIF read MUC1, and a TA-MUC1 clone would answer a different question.

exclusion_reason: Retracted (PubMed publication type 'Retracted Publication'); its MUC1-C/MDR1 findings in urothelial carcinoma cannot be relied on.
intervention_label: MUC1-C inhibition in cisplatin-resistant urothelial carcinoma
PRAME peptide/HLA-A*02:01-directed TCR-mimic antibody (Pr20)
model_system: PRAME-positive/HLA-A2-positive human cancer and leukemia lines; mouse xenograft models of human leukemia
control_arm: PRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative lines; unmodified IgG1 versus afucosylated Fc
mechanism: An antibody shaped like a TCR binds the PRAME300-309 (ALYVDSLFFL) peptide presented on HLA-A*02:01, converting an intracellular antigen into a surface target.
key_finding: Pr20 bound PRAME-positive HLA-A2-positive cancers, and the afucosylated form drove ADCC and was effective in leukemia xenografts. Binding rose sharply after IFN-γ exposure through induction of the immunoproteasome subunit β5i, which spares the ALY epitope from destructive internal cleavage.
caveats: Leukemia xenografts, not solid tumor, and Pr20 is not brenetafusp. Two transferable points: the epitope is presented at very low copy number, and its density is IFN-γ-dependent — so a PRAME-directed agent's target may vary with the inflammatory state of the lesion, not only with PRAME transcript level.

intervention_label: PRAME425/HLA-A*02:01-directed TCR bispecific engager and TCR T cells
model_system: NUT carcinoma cell line panel, patient-derived xenograft, tissue microarray, and targeted immunopeptidomics with labeled peptide standards
n_units: n=5 cell lines; n=77 tissue microarray samples; n=165 sequenced patient samples
control_arm: PRAME-negative and HLA-A2-negative targets; BRD4::NUTM1 knockout versus parental
mechanism: A TCR-based bispecific modeled on brenetafusp engages the HLA-A*02:01/SLLQHLIGL (PRAME425) complex and redirects CD3 to lyse the presenting cell.
key_finding: Targeted mass spectrometry detected the PRAME425 epitope in all four HLA-A*02-positive, PRAME-positive samples tested, at higher levels than the PRAME312 or PRAME462 epitopes. Both the brenetafusp-modeled bispecific and PRAME425 TCR T cells produced T-cell-mediated killing of PRAME-positive cells.
caveats: NUT carcinoma, a fusion-driven tumor whose PRAME expression is oncogene-driven; nothing here says urothelial carcinoma presents PRAME425 at comparable density. It does show the epitope is directly measurable by mass spectrometry, which is a sharper readout than IHC if PRAME imaging comes back equivocal.

intervention_label: PRAME-specific TCR T cells with a PD1-41BB chimeric costimulatory receptor
model_system: PRAME-positive tumor lines with repetitive rechallenge in vitro; PD-L1-positive melanoma xenograft in mice
control_arm: PRAME TCR T cells without the PD1-41BB receptor
dose_and_schedule: single infusion of TCR T cells
mechanism: A high-sensitivity PRAME TCR isolated from non-tolerized repertoires drives killing, while a PD1-41BB switch receptor converts PD-L1 engagement from inhibition into costimulation.
key_finding: Adding PD1-41BB increased IFN-γ secretion and cytotoxicity and prevented exhaustion under repetitive tumor rechallenge, without changing the in-vitro safety profile. A single dose cleared a PD-L1-positive melanoma xenograft that TCR T cells alone could not.
caveats: Melanoma xenografts in immunodeficient mice, so the switch-receptor benefit is measured against tumor PD-L1 only, with no host immune contribution. IMA203 as trialed does not carry this receptor.

exclusion_reason: Preprint of the peer-reviewed publication already logged (PMID 41644270); same data, duplicate citation.
intervention_label: PRAME epitopes in NUT carcinoma (bioRxiv preprint)
H2-scDb (TP53 R175H/HLA-A*02:01-directed bispecific single-chain diabody)
model_system: human cancer cell lines presenting p53 R175H on HLA-A*02:01, with T cells, and mouse xenograft models
control_arm: wild-type TP53 and HLA-A2-negative cell lines
mechanism: An antibody selected against the HMTEVVRHC peptide bound to HLA-A*02:01 is built into a bispecific diabody that also engages CD3, redirecting T cells against a mutant-p53-derived neoantigen.
key_finding: The antibody bound the mutant peptide-HLA complex with specificity resolved structurally, discriminating R175H from wild-type sequence. Despite very low peptide-HLA copy number on the cancer cell surface, the bispecific activated T cells to lyse antigen-presenting cancer cells in vitro and in mice.
caveats: Cell lines and xenografts, no urothelial model, and no clinical publication exists for CLSP-1025 — this paper and its successors are the entire evidence base for that trial. This patient's R175H was seen in plasma ctDNA at 0.09% VAF, so whether the current tumor clone even carries it is unestablished.

intervention_label: TP53 R175H/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific antibodies versus CAR T cells — affinity requirements
model_system: higher-affinity H2 scFv variants from phage biopanning, tested as bispecific antibodies and as CD28z CAR, CD3γ and TCR formats; mouse xenograft models
control_arm: parental H2 scFv affinity variant across each format
mechanism: Raising scFv affinity for the p53 R175H peptide-HLA complex changes engager potency and receptor function in opposite directions, because a CAR's serial engagement depends on release from a low-density antigen.
key_finding: Bispecific antibody killing and xenograft tumor control improved as affinity moved into the low nanomolar range, with specificity preserved. The same higher-affinity binders reduced function in every CAR format tested, through weaker T-cell activation on contact.
caveats: Xenografts only. Read alongside the disclosure that the senior group founded Clasp Therapeutics, this is the direct preclinical lineage of the CLSP-1025 engager, and it argues that the engager format — not a CAR — is the right one at this antigen density.

intervention_label: Co-STAR receptors against the p53 neoantigen at low antigen density
model_system: cancer cells titrated for peptide-HLA density in vitro; mouse tumor models
control_arm: conventional CARs and patient-derived TCRs against the same p53 neoantigen
mechanism: A receptor combining a TCR-mimic antibody fragment for recognition with MyD88 and CD40 modules for NF-κB costimulation, sitting between a CAR's affinity and a TCR's sensitivity.
key_finding: Co-STAR T cells killed cells bearing low antigen densities better than conventional CARs or patient-derived TCRs. In mice, Co-STARs gave greater T-cell expansion and more durable regressions than TCRs carrying the same MyD88/CD40 costimulation.
caveats: Preclinical only, and no Co-STAR product is in a trial this patient could enter. It quantifies the shared obstacle for every p53-neoantigen agent — copy number on the cell surface — which is the reason the CLSP-1025 and NT-175 packages should be read as one problem rather than two.

intervention_label: TP53 R175H-directed TCR T cells and p53-reactive tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes
model_system: whole-exome screening of metastatic solid tumors with immunologic identification of reactive T cells; TCR-transduced cells tested in vitro and in vivo
n_units: n=163 patients sequenced; n=78 with TP53 missense mutation; 21 unique T-cell reactivities; 39 TCRs
control_arm: autologous TIL without p53 reactivity; HLA-mismatched and wild-type TP53 targets
mechanism: TCRs isolated against shared TP53 hotspot neoantigens recognize the mutant peptide only in the context of the matching HLA allele, making the pair — not the mutation alone — the eligibility gate.
key_finding: A library of 39 TCRs covered TP53 mutations shared by 7.3% of patients with solid tumors, recognizing tumor in a mutation- and HLA-specific way. Autologous TIL infused into 12 patients gave only 2 partial responses, with low-frequency, exhausted, poorly persisting p53-reactive cells; one patient given peripheral blood lymphocytes transduced with an HLA-A*02-restricted p53 R175H TCR had a 55% regression lasting 6 months.
caveats: PubMed types this record as an editorial/comment, which is a metadata error — the text is a primary report. The single R175H/HLA-A*02 TCR-transduced patient is the closest human precedent for NT-175 and the transient response is the honest ceiling to quote; it also shows why an engineered TCR product beat unselected TIL.

intervention_label: p53 neoantigen-reactive T cells recovered from peripheral blood
model_system: sorted antigen-experienced peripheral blood lymphocytes from patients with TP53-mutant tumors, stimulated in vitro against p53 neoantigens; tumor cell line recognition assays
control_arm: patients without TIL reactivity to mutated TP53; wild-type p53 and HLA-mismatched targets
mechanism: Antigen-experienced circulating T cells mirror the intratumoral p53-neoantigen repertoire, so blood can substitute for tumor as the starting material for identifying reactive TCRs.
key_finding: All five patients with p53-reactive TIL had matching reactivity in blood, and the four without TIL reactivity had none in blood either. One culture was 78% reactive against p53 R175H on HLA-A*02:01, and TP53-mutation-specific T cells recognized tumor lines carrying the right HLA and mutation, confirming natural processing and presentation.
caveats: Small patient numbers and no clinical outcome. Directly useful given this case's tissue scarcity: banked PBMCs and apheresis could be screened for R175H/HLA-A*02:01 reactivity without spending the one fresh-frozen tumor vial.

intervention_label: lymph-node-targeted amphiphile peptide vaccine boosting of TCR T cells
model_system: established murine solid tumors refractory to TCR T-cell monotherapy; human TCR T cells against NY-ESO-1, mutant KRAS and HPV16 E7 in vitro
control_arm: TCR T cells alone; vaccine alone
dose_and_schedule: amphiphile-conjugated cognate peptide plus adjuvant given after TCR T-cell transfer, without lymphodepletion
mechanism: Amphiphile conjugation traffics peptide and adjuvant to draining lymph nodes, where transferred T cells are re-stimulated in situ and the endogenous repertoire is recruited alongside them.
key_finding: Vaccine plus TCR T cells eradicated tumors that TCR T cells alone could not, with expansion of both the transferred cells and the endogenous antitumor repertoire and no lymphodepletion. Durable protection tracked with antigen spreading to tumor antigens the vaccine did not encode.
caveats: Murine tumors plus in-vitro human confirmation; no cancer-patient data. It is the mechanistic argument for sequencing this patient's ongoing neoantigen vaccine with a TIL or TCR T product rather than running them as separate programs.

intervention_label: neoantigen vaccine efficacy as a function of antigen localization and CD4 help
model_system: syngeneic mouse tumors engineered to express membrane-localized or cytoplasmic neoantigens; pan-cancer TCGA analysis of intratumoral IgG
control_arm: cytoplasmic versus membrane-localized version of the same neoantigen; CD8-depleted and Fc-receptor-deficient arms
mechanism: Membrane-exposed neoantigens elicit class-switched IgG that engages Fc receptors and myeloid cells, a CD4-dependent arm of vaccine efficacy that runs alongside the CD8 response.
key_finding: Membrane-localized but not cytoplasmic neoantigens drove class-switched IgG, myeloid activation and tumor restriction independent of CD8 T cells, requiring CD4 help, antigen-specific IgG and Fc engagement. A Trop2 T256R mutant with impaired membrane localization failed to elicit comparable vaccine-induced control, and CXCL13 or IL-21 co-expression amplified the antibody arm.
caveats: Engineered syngeneic models with defined antigens, far from a 24-peptide personalized program. Relevant because this patient's EliSpot response is CD4-skewed (2 of 14 pools) and currently read as a weak signal — this model gives CD4-dominant responses a plausible effector route, and predicts that where the epitope sits on the protein matters.

intervention_label: CTLA-4 plus PD-1/PD-L1 blockade — intratumoral mechanism of the doublet
model_system: B16.SIY murine melanoma
control_arm: single-agent anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-L1 or IDO inhibition; FTY720-treated mice to block lymphocyte egress
dose_and_schedule: permutations of anti-CTLA-4 mAb, anti-PD-L1 mAb and the IDO inhibitor INCB23843
mechanism: The doublet acts on T cells already inside the tumor, restoring IL-2 production and proliferation, rather than by priming new T cells in draining lymph nodes.
key_finding: All three doublets improved tumor control over single agents, with complete rejection in many mice and no vaccine or adoptive transfer. Priming in draining nodes rose only minimally, while tumor-infiltrating CD8 T cells regained IL-2 production and proliferation by day 3; blocking new T-cell trafficking with FTY720 preserved most of the effect.
caveats: A single immunogenic murine melanoma line, and the mice were checkpoint-naive. This patient progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance, so the relevant question is whether an exhausted intratumoral pool still responds to CTLA-4 addition — which this model does not test.

intervention_label: [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46-I (albumin-binder FAP radioligand)
model_system: U87MG (high FAP) and HT-1080 (low FAP) tumor-bearing mice; SPECT/CT and radioligand therapy studies
control_arm: [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46 without the albumin binder; vehicle
mechanism: An albumin-binding moiety prolongs blood residence, raising tumor accumulation and dose delivered per administration; killing is by beta emission across the FAP-positive compartment rather than by receptor signaling.
key_finding: Binding affinity was preserved (IC50 1.5 ± 0.3 nM) while tumor accumulation and retention rose over the parent ligand. The albumin-binder version suppressed and shrank tumors where the parent [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-46 did not.
caveats: Glioblastoma and fibrosarcoma xenografts where FAP is on the tumor cells themselves, not the stromal-FAP configuration seen on this patient's MXIF. The gating problem is upstream anyway: the only FAPi PET on record showed uptake in BCG-granulomatous prostate tissue and no FAP-avid urothelial carcinoma.

intervention_label: [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-2P(FAPI)2 radioligand therapy with PD-L1 blockade
model_system: CT26-FAP syngeneic mouse tumors; immunohistochemistry and single-cell RNA sequencing of the treated microenvironment
control_arm: radioligand alone, anti-PD-L1 alone, and untreated mice; 68Ga versus 177Lu label
mechanism: FAP-targeted beta emission causes double-strand breaks and raises tumor PD-L1, converting the stromal compartment into an adjuvant for checkpoint blockade.
key_finding: 177Lu-DOTA-2P(FAPI)2 induced double-strand breaks and upregulated PD-L1 more effectively than the 68Ga label. Combined with anti-PD-L1 it eliminated tumors, and rechallenged mice showed complete rejection; single-cell analysis showed more infiltrating CD8 T cells, fewer regulatory T cells, and a contribution from mature neutrophils.
caveats: CT26 colorectal cells engineered to express FAP, so the model bypasses the question of whether native stromal FAP delivers enough dose. It offers a mechanistic reason to pair FAP radioligand with checkpoint blockade if imaging ever confirms FAP-avid urothelial disease, and nothing more.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition as synthetic lethality in ARID1A-deficient tumors
model_system: isogenic and naturally ARID1A-mutant tumor cell lines in vitro, with in-vivo confirmation
control_arm: ARID1A-proficient isogenic cells
dose_and_schedule: clinical-stage ATR inhibitors, in vitro and in vivo
mechanism: ARID1A loss produces topoisomerase 2A and cell-cycle defects that leave the cell dependent on ATR checkpoint activity; removing ATR forces premature mitotic entry.
key_finding: ARID1A defects sensitized tumor cells to ATR inhibitors in vitro and in vivo. In ARID1A-mutant cells, ATR inhibition triggered premature mitotic entry, genomic instability and apoptosis.
caveats: No urothelial model, and the case's ARID1A alteration is reported without zygosity or protein-loss confirmation — the biomarker in these experiments is ARID1A deficiency, not the presence of a mutation call. This is the original rationale behind the ATR-inhibitor trials on the list (ART0380, tuvusertib) and remains hypothesis-grade for this patient.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition in ARID1A-deficient cells — KLF5 as a modifier
model_system: genome-scale CRISPR screens in ARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-proficient cells under ATR inhibition
control_arm: ARID1A-proficient isogenic cells; untreated screen arm
mechanism: KLF5 protects against replication stress partly by regulating BRD4 recruitment to chromatin, so KLF5 loss compounds the replication stress that ARID1A deficiency already imposes.
key_finding: KLF5 loss severely reduced fitness of ARID1A-deficient cells and sensitized ARID1A-proficient cells to ATR inhibition. The mechanism ran through replication stress, DNA damage, DNA-RNA hybrid accumulation and genomic instability on ATR inhibition.
caveats: Screen-based and in-vitro only. Its practical use in this case is as a caution rather than a lead: ATR-inhibitor response in an ARID1A-mutant tumor is modified by other genes, so a single ARID1A call is a thin basis for predicting benefit.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition with temozolomide in ARID1A-mutated cancers
model_system: ARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-proficient cancer cells; ovarian tumor xenografts carrying ARID1A mutations
control_arm: temozolomide alone, PARP inhibitor alone, ARID1A-proficient cells
dose_and_schedule: temozolomide combined with PARP inhibitor, in vitro and in xenografts
mechanism: ARID1A deficiency leaves accumulated DNA base lesions and abasic sites with delayed long-patch base excision repair, so adding a methylating agent to PARP trapping converts unrepaired lesions into double-strand breaks.
key_finding: ARID1A-deficient cells accumulated base lesions and abasic sites and recruited long-patch BER effectors slowly. Temozolomide alone was inactive, but combined with a PARP inhibitor it produced double-strand breaks, replication stress and fork instability, and significantly delayed growth of ARID1A-mutant ovarian xenografts.
caveats: Ovarian models and a combination with no urothelial trial behind it. The negative half is the useful half: PARP inhibitor monotherapy was not the active arm, which argues against reading ARID1A loss as a PARP-inhibitor indication on its own.

intervention_label: EZH2 inhibition in ARID1A-deficient cancer
model_system: ARID1A-deficient and ARID1A-wild-type gastric cancer cell lines, including ARID1A knockdown; cell viability and colony formation
control_arm: ARID1A-wild-type parental lines
dose_and_schedule: EZH2 inhibitors across a dose range
mechanism: Loss of the SWI/SNF subunit ARID1A leaves the tumor dependent on PRC2/EZH2-driven repression, with PI3K/AKT signaling as the downstream survival axis.
key_finding: EZH2 inhibitors reduced viability of ARID1A-deficient cells dose-dependently and selectively relative to ARID1A-wild-type cells. ARID1A knockdown raised phosphorylated AKT, and EZH2 downregulation normalized PI3K/AKT signaling in the deficient cells.
caveats: In vitro only, no xenograft arm, gastric rather than urothelial. No EZH2-inhibitor trial appears on this case's list, so it stays as background for the synthetic-lethality axis rather than a route to an option.

exclusion_reason: Bladder-specific and mechanistically adjacent, but the biomarker tested is ATM loss rather than ARID1A; the patient's ATM status is not in the available record, so it supports no ranked option.
intervention_label: ATM deficiency and DNA repair-targeted vulnerabilities in bladder cancer
